response: The fundamental bottleneck in local AI inference and training has long been the memory capacity of the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). In a conventional discrete GPU (dGPU) architecture, the processor and its memory are physically separate entities. The GPU relies on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) or GDDR, which is soldered directly to the GPU package. While this memory offers extremely high bandwidth—often exceeding 1,000 GB/s—it is limited in capacity, typically ranging from 12 GB to 80 GB for consumer and professional cards, respectively.
